title: EFFECTS OF REVERBERATION TIME AND SOUND SOURCE COMPOSITION ON SENSE OF PLACE CASE STUDY IN PRIVATE OFFICES
research_question: Can reverberation time influence place attachment, identity, and dependence? Can background noise in a sound source composition influence place attachment, identity, and dependence? Can sound signals in a sound source composition influence place attachment, identity, and dependence? Can Absolute Magnitude Estimation scale (AME) be used as a prediction tool for place indicators? Can reverberation time influence place indicators? Can background noise in a sound source composition influence place indicators? Can sound signals in a sound source composition influence place indicators?

participants.description: 15 academic members from the Faculty of Architecture in Çankaya University, who had been using their private offices for at least one year. Offices were designed for one or two users, faced northern or southern directions, had access to a window and corridor, and were naturally or artificially illuminated.
participants.recruitment: Not explicitly stated, but implies faculty members from Çankaya University.

stimuli_or_exposures.description: 9 acoustic conditions: 1 original office environment (headset-free) and 8 simulated audio samples (headset-based). Simulated samples varied in reverberation time (0.8s, 1.2s) and sound source composition (familiar/unfamiliar background noise, specific sound signals like footsteps, door knocking, chair, door, locker, drawer).

measures.construct: Sense of Place (Place Attachment, Place Identity, Place Dependence)
measures.instrument: 7-point Likert scale questionnaire (9 statements, 3 per construct)

measures.construct: Place Indicators (Emotions, Orientation for Place Attachment; Meaning, Character for Place Identity; Expectation, Advantage for Place Dependence)
measures.instrument: Absolute Magnitude Estimation (AME) scale (participants assigned positive numbers to descriptors)

findings.consequent: Sense of Place (average of three constructs) (SoP questionnaire)
findings.mechanism: Attention effect: unfamiliar stimuli attract more attention, making it easier to focus on other dimensions. Also, lower sensory detection threshold for familiar stimuli and participants' expectations.

findings.consequent: Place constructs evaluation (SoP questionnaire)
findings.mechanism: Bias towards original conditions due to time spent experiencing the space and headset-free evaluation. Simulated conditions showed a prerogative for place attachment's 'willingness to make this place even better'.
findings.quote: Place constructs were evaluated more uniformly in the original condition. The higher mean of PA1 “I am happy working in this place” is competing with other means from other statements in each construct. However, simulated conditions showed an obvious prerogative of place attachment’s PA2 “I am willing to make this place even better”.

findings.consequent: Place indicators evaluation (AME method)
findings.mechanism: AME method provided more homogenous results in both conditions, suggesting that specifying indicators directs users' attention to different aspects of the environment, making it more adaptable for short-term experimental conditions.
findings.quote: Compared with place constructs evaluated by the sense of place questionnaire, the results of the place indicators measured by the AME method are more homogenous in both conditions.

mechanisms: Longer reverberation times create a more active, responsive, and higher-ambient-noise spaces, which participants may expect from an educational office environment.

Unfamiliar background noise enhances sense of place due to an attention effect, where novel stimuli draw more attention, or due to participants' expectations and lower sensory detection thresholds for familiar stimuli.

Sound signals like footsteps and knocking, especially those with rhythmic amplitudes and high frequencies (around 5 kHz), negatively influence sense of place by signaling approaching presence or territorial penetration, drawing attention to external activities.

The Absolute Magnitude Estimation (AME) method directs users' attention to specific place indicators, influencing their evaluation and making it more adaptable for short-term experimental conditions compared to general questionnaires.

Psychoacoustical parameters (loudness, pitch, timbre) derived from sound signals' amplitude, frequency, and temporal distribution influence the perception of occurrences, sound source location, and suitability of the environment, thereby affecting sense of place.

Multisensory perception plays a role; the auditory stimulus's effect on sense of place can be influenced by other stimuli (temperature, visual setting, lighting), and a lack of holistic experience (auditory-biased experiment) may diminish the sense of place.
implementation_implications: The interactions and correlations between room acoustics and sense of place should be considered in architectural design.
Room acoustics can enhance or diminish participants' attachment to place, give meaning to place, and influence dependence on place.

limitations: Small sample size (15 participants) due to recently emerged health problems.
All participants were from the faculty of architecture, potentially introducing bias as they might be more familiar with the concept of sense of place.
Limited types of spaces investigated (only private offices); future studies should compare with other spaces and those with special acoustic demands.
Questionnaire translation from English to Turkish was almost literal, potentially missing or adding aspects to the sense of place concept.
Limited physical parameters investigated (only reverberation time and sound source composition); other acoustics and psychoacoustics parameters are equally essential.
Psychoacoustics parameters were analyzed generally by simple observation of sound signals' spectrograms, suggesting a need for more in-depth study.

The experiment was generally auditory-biased, as users used headsets, lacking a holistic multisensory experience; future studies should use VR, AR, or similar Soundlab settings for more holistic experiences.
